subject: Week 38: build the preschool long-list — tours open in September

content.hook: build the preschool long-list — tours open in September
content.thisWeek: Receptive language is the story of days 264 through 270: he likely understands 20 to 50 words and follows a simple command or two, while production may be one to three specific words or none at all — the CDC 2022 revision places words beyond mama and dada at the 15-month checkpoint. Cruising is fluid for many and standing alone briefly is emerging for some, both CDC 12-month checkpoints rather than requirements today. Cognitively he searches for hidden objects and uses objects the way they are meant to be used: cup to mouth, brush to hair.
watchFors: [low concern] Early negotiation behavior — pointing at what he wants, protesting when it does not arrive. Testing the limit is cognitive progress, not defiance.
[low concern] A cold cycling through the house in the middle of RSV and influenza season — supportive care only; no over-the-counter cough or cold medicine under age 2.
[monitor] No babbling, or babble without consonant variety, heading into the 12-month visit — write down examples now rather than reconstructing them later.
[call within 24h] A cold that worsens after day five, new wheezing, or resting breathing faster than 60 breaths a minute.
[call now] Fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, labored breathing with retractions or nasal flaring, or blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

enrichment.body: Build the preschool long-list this month, then close the tab. Pull the ISSFBA directory, note the per-school application fees ($50 to $100 across eight to 10 schools), and calendar September 2027 — tour season for the fall he turns 2, with applications due that January and him at 16 to 20 months on the tours. No school takes an application under about 18 months and tour slots reset annually, so touring before roughly 14 months buys nothing.

Probe comprehension once a day with your hands still: say give me the ball without pointing, and watch what happens. Receptive vocabulary leads expressive by one to three months in year one, so what he understands is the better read on progress right now.

Move hand-held walking outdoors onto uneven ground — grass, sand, a gentle slope. Varied surfaces force the ankle and hip corrections a flat hallway never asks for, and hand-held stepping is the rehearsal that runs while balance catches up.
Trade one bedtime story for a single-word naming book, name each image, then stop talking for two seconds. The pause is what converts labeling into a turn he can take.

upcoming: Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — 16 days left. If it is done, close the loop on the iron rescreen and influenza #2 if this is his first flu season; if not, take any slot offered this week.
Day 270-365 (Feb 5–May 11, 2027): preschool list-building window opens Friday — the long-list and one September calendar entry are the whole required action.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit due by the first birthday — ask for the referral at the next visit and book the spring slot.

subject: Week 39: answer every gesture — waving and giving are pre-word turns

content.hook: answer every gesture — waving and giving are pre-word turns
content.thisWeek: Days 271 through 277 close the third quarter. Gesture is where the growth shows: waving bye, shaking his head, arms up to be lifted, handing over an object when you ask — the CDC scores waving and giving on the 12-month checklist, so early appearance is a bonus rather than the bar. Cruising is fluid for many, first independent steps arrive for a few, and first specific words are emerging for some, with the CDC 2022 checkpoint for words beyond mama and dada at 15 months.
watchFors: [low concern] Bumps and knocks from cruising falls onto carpet — supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces are how the balance system calibrates.
[low concern] Waking early to stand up in the crib — drop the mattress to its lowest setting if you have not already, and keep the response short and boring.
[monitor] No joint attention — he does not follow your point or bring you things to look at — alongside flat, unvaried babble. Two channels quiet at once is the pattern worth documenting.
[call within 24h] A stomach bug with fewer than five wet diapers in 24 hours, or vomiting that persists past 12 hours.
[call now] Severe respiratory distress — retractions, grunting, nasal flaring — or fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy; blue lips or unresponsiveness is 911.

enrichment.body: Wave at every arrival and departure and say the word with it — hello on the way in, bye-bye on the way out, the same script from both parents. Waving is a CDC 1-year item and it is acquired by imitation, not instruction.

Put words on the gestures he already owns: arms up becomes up, a head shake becomes all done, an offered toy becomes thank you. Mapping language onto a signal he already controls is easier than asking him to learn both at once, and it keeps the exchange bidirectional — turns, not volume, are what the language data support.

Introduce a single-shape knob puzzle — one large piece, one hole. Removing and replacing the piece is a spatial and fine-motor task right at the edge of what he can do, and the knob is what makes it reachable with a thumb-and-finger grip.

Bank one outdoor block a day through the wet stretch — a carrier walk or a blanket on the playground grass. It costs nothing, delivers vestibular and visual input a living room cannot, and hands you a 30-minute narration slot.

upcoming: Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — nine days left in the window. If the visit is behind you, chase the loose ends this week: hemoglobin result, influenza #2 if this is his first season, and anything the ASQ-3 screen flagged.
Day 280 (Mon Feb 15, 2027): the window closes and the next scheduled well visit is at 12 months — anything arising between now and May routes through a sick visit or the triage line.

subject: Week 40: 50% walk by 12 months, 90% by 15 — pad the landing zone

content.hook: 50% walk by 12 months, 90% by 15 — pad the landing zone
content.thisWeek: Days 278 through 284 open the final quarter, and walking is now the dominant motor question: roughly 50% of infants walk by 12 months, 75% by 14, and 90% by 15. The CDC moved its walks-alone checkpoint to 15 months in the 2022 revision, so a non-walker at the first birthday sits squarely inside the distribution. Expect fluid cruising, brief unsupported stands for some (CDC checkpoint: 12 months), and more elaborate imitation — stirring with a spoon, pushing a car across the floor.
watchFors: [low concern] Several falls a day during practice. The target is supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces, not zero falls.
[low concern] Head bonks against furniture edges — the fall is not the hazard, the corner is; pad the coffee table and the hearth this week.
[monitor] Persistent inability to bear weight through his legs when you hold him upright — this one goes to the pediatrician directly rather than into the notes file.
[call within 24h] New wheezing, or an illness that plateaus instead of improving — RSV and influenza run through March here.
[call now] Head injury followed by persistent vomiting, unusual lethargy, or any loss of consciousness; fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

enrichment.body: Re-audit the house at standing height: pad the hearth and coffee-table corners, add window guards on anything above ground level (screens are not weight-bearing), and put pinch guards on doors he can swing shut. The last audit was run for a baby who could not reach a tabletop.

Practice stairs upward with you seated one step behind him — two or three carpeted steps, up only, daily. Stair climbing trains the same hip and ankle control walking needs, and it is the skill that prevents the fall down them later.

Hand him the real object instead of the toy version — a soft brush for his own hair, a wooden spoon in an empty bowl, a cloth for his tray. Using objects for their intended purpose is the CDC 12-month cognitive item, and copying your actual routines is how he gets there.

Write the sick-day plan down before you need it: who takes the fever call, which backup-care benefit you actually have, and the 24-hour fever-free return rule most centers run. Infants in group care average 8 to 12 illnesses in year one, at a parental cost of roughly five to 10 missed workdays.

upcoming: Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — the window closes Monday. If the visit happened, the only open items should be the iron result and influenza #2; if it did not, call Monday morning and take a late slot.
Day 285-291 (Feb 20-26, 2027): first outdoor shoes become relevant if he is walking outside — flexible soles only, and barefoot stays the indoor default.
Day 364-380 (May 10-26, 2027): 12-month well visit — the next scheduled well visit once Monday's window closes.

subject: Week 41: narrate the whole day — first words run on input, not drills

content.hook: narrate the whole day — first words run on input, not drills
content.thisWeek: Days 285 through 291: self-feeding is more refined, most soft family foods are on the table, and he can drink from a cup with help. Cruising is fluent for many and first steps arrive for some — the CDC walks-alone checkpoint stays at 15 months. Expressive vocabulary right now can be zero to five words and both ends sit inside the range; the growth is on the receptive side, and it responds to input volume and back-and-forth rather than to drilling.
watchFors: [low concern] Refusal of foods he ate happily last month — preference churn is standard here; keep offering the rejected food without pressure or substitution.
[low concern] No words at all. About 25% of 12-month-olds are not yet using words, and the CDC checkpoint for words beyond mama and dada is 15 months.
[monitor] Rich babble but no gestures — no waving, no showing, no arms up. The gesture channel carries more weight than word count at this age.
[call within 24h] Night waking with crying plus ear-pulling after a cold, or fever above 102F rectal with ear drainage — otitis media peaks between 6 and 24 months.
[call now] Fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, or respiratory distress with retractions or grunting; blue lips or unresponsiveness is 911.

enrichment.body: Narrate the two hours you are with him most — bath, dinner prep, the walk — and name what he is already looking at instead of redirecting him to what you wanted to name. Words that land on the object he chose get mapped faster, and pausing after every sound he makes turns narration into the conversational turns that predicted language-network activation years later.

Teach the way down: from standing at the couch, guide his hands toward the floor and let his knees fold. Getting down is a separate skill from getting up, and it is the one that prevents the stiff backward fall.

Move him onto the family menu with three rules: soft enough to squash between thumb and finger, cut smaller than a marble, and nothing round left whole — grapes quartered lengthwise, no whole nuts, no popcorn, no hot-dog coins.

Buy outdoor shoes only once he is actually walking outside: a sole you can twist, a thumb-width of room at the toe, no ankle support. Indoors stays barefoot, which is still the better surface for balance learning.

upcoming: Day 280 (Feb 15, 2027) has passed and the 9-month visit window is closed — if the visit never happened, book it now as a late well visit rather than waiting for the 12-month slot.
Day 292-298 (Feb 27–Mar 5, 2027): 11-month landmark — open the 12-month visit notes file then: word list, sleep pattern, eating range, motor checkpoints.

subject: Week 42: start the 12-month visit file — four things to write down

content.hook: start the 12-month visit file — four things to write down
content.thisWeek: Days 292 through 298 mark 11 months, the point where infant becomes toddler in the literal sense of the word. Receptive vocabulary is running roughly 50 to 100 words against an expressive count of zero to 10, and that gap is the normal shape of this month rather than a lag. Motor: cruising and furniture-walking for many (CDC checkpoint: 12 months) and three to 10 independent steps for some, with the walks-alone checkpoint at 15 months; socially, peekaboo is reliable and pat-a-cake is emerging on the 1-year checklist.
watchFors: [low concern] Separation distress at drop-off and a brief return of bedtime resistance — keep the handoff short and the routine identical, and it resolves on its own.
[monitor] No babble, no joint attention, and no interest in shared games, all three at once — that combination belongs in front of the pediatrician; the absence of words alone does not.
[monitor] A consistent one-sided preference when cruising or stepping, or a limp. Asymmetry is worth a look even though a slow overall pace is not.
[call within 24h] Illness that persists past three days, or a fever that returns after a clear day.
[call now] Severe respiratory distress, fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, or blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

enrichment.body: Open the 12-month visit file and add to it daily: the running word list including approximations, the sleep pattern, the eating range, and where he stands on the motor checkpoints. Two months of notes beats recall in the exam room, and this visit carries five vaccines plus hemoglobin and lead screening.

Close the baby-sign question before the practical window ends Mar 7 — free at home is the only version worth running, since the one longitudinal RCT found no language acceleration and a 17-study review supports no developmental claims. The ceiling is less frustration, not faster speech.
enrichment.sourceLabel: Hanen Centre on baby sign evidence

enrichment.body: Play peekaboo and pat-a-cake on a fixed script — same words, same pauses, every time. Both sit on the CDC 1-year checklist, and the predictability is what lets him anticipate his turn and take it.

Cut the book rotation down to three titles and repeat them. Repetition is what converts a heard word into a mapped one at this stage, and he will start turning to the page he wants before he can name what is on it.

upcoming: Day 364-380 (May 10-26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR, varicella, hepatitis A, PCV #4 and the Hib booster, plus hemoglobin and lead screening. The booking call goes out in late March; the notes file starts this week.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit due by the first birthday — the AAP dental home starts at age one, so book the spring appointment when you book the 12-month visit.
